_note: This page restates numbers that belong to three other pages, so every claim re-runs against THAT page's own shipped data file as well as against this page's derived one. A correction on the funding map, the occupations page or the federal-money page fails this gate instead of leaving a stale board figure behind. Paths climb out of scorecard/data/ on purpose. Two claims here guard an ABSENCE rather than a figure — sc-empty-slots and sc-context-separate — because the defect this page exists to prevent is a plausible number appearing in a cell nobody measured.

claims.text: Headline and hero card 1: public records fill eight of the fifteen rows PIC answers for, none of the four on membership and revenue, and the other seven are defined and left empty.
claims.source: scorecard/data/scorecard.json, written by scorecard/derive_scorecard.py from the four source datasets listed in this file
claims.assert: D['sc']['counts']['public'] == 8 and D['sc']['counts']['accountable'] == 15 and D['sc']['counts']['vault'] == 7 and D['sc']['counts']['public'] + D['sc']['counts']['vault'] == D['sc']['counts']['accountable'] and len([r for r in D['sc']['rows'] if r['group'] == 'A']) == 4 and all(r['status'] == 'vault' for r in D['sc']['rows'] if r['group'] == 'A')
claims.actual: (D['sc']['counts'], [r['status'] for r in D['sc']['rows'] if r['group'] == 'A'])
claims.falsified_if: A row is added to or removed from any group, or a group-A row acquires a public source. The headline prints both halves of the fraction, so either number moving breaks it. The four-on-membership-and-revenue clause is the group-A test: if a dues or renewal figure ever becomes publishable from a public record, the sentence is wrong even though the arithmetic still holds.

claims.text: Every row sourced from PIC's own registers renders as 'not published here' and carries no figure, and every row not so sourced carries one.
claims.source: scorecard/data/scorecard.json — the same condition derive_scorecard.py raises on at build time and app.js throws on at render time
claims.assert: all(r['current'] is None and r['sub'] is None for r in D['sc']['rows'] if r['status'] == 'vault') and all(r['current'] for r in D['sc']['rows'] if r['status'] != 'vault') and len([r for r in D['sc']['rows'] if r['status'] == 'vault']) == 7
claims.actual: [(r['id'], r['current']) for r in D['sc']['rows'] if r['status'] == 'vault']
claims.falsified_if: Any vault row acquires a value, including a zero, a dash, a range or a placeholder. This is the one failure the page exists to prevent, so the tolerance is not a band: a vault cell holds nothing at all. It also fails in the other direction, if a row marked public or context ever renders blank.

claims.text: Hero card 2, row b-assigned and the closer: $79.2 million of the $85.3 million awarded, 92.8 percent, has a named recipient in the register. The row's definition says a named recipient is an organisation or one of the two programme aggregates, whose $23,094,356 is in the numerator (corrected 2026-09-29 from "naming the organisation that holds them"). How much of it is on an executed line is sc-executed.
claims.source: PIC award register as of 13 August 2026, via funding-map/data/funding.json; recomputed here rather than read from a total
claims.assert: sum(a['amount'] for r in D['fm']['recipients'] for a in r['awards']) == 79170176 and D['fm']['meta']['totals']['awards'] == 85335784 and D['sc']['delivery']['assigned'] == sum(a['amount'] for r in D['fm']['recipients'] for a in r['awards']) and D['sc']['delivery']['awarded'] == D['fm']['meta']['totals']['awards'] and round(D['sc']['delivery']['assigned'] / D['sc']['delivery']['awarded'] * 100, 1) == 92.8 and sum(a['amount'] for r in D['fm']['recipients'] if r['id'] in ('polymer-pilot-facility', 'regional-workforce') for a in r['awards']) == 23094356 and (lambda df: 'naming the organisation' not in df and 'programme aggregate' in df and all(n in df for n in ('Polymer Pilot Facility', 'regional workforce programs'))) (one(r for r in D['sc']['rows'] if r['id'] == 'b-assigned')['definition'])
claims.actual: (sum(a['amount'] for r in D['fm']['recipients'] for a in r['awards']), D['fm']['meta']['totals']['awards'])
claims.falsified_if: A recipient line is added, removed or restated in the register, or the award total moves. The share is printed to a tenth of a percent, so 92.74 or 92.85 breaks it. The claim is about ASSIGNMENT, not payment: it would survive unchanged if not one dollar had been disbursed, which is exactly why the disbursement row beneath it is empty.

claims.text: Hero standfirst, band B lede, the EDA bar's label, the chart's source line, rows b-assigned, b-eda and b-disbursed: $73.2 million of the $79.2 million with a named recipient is on an executed line. The other $5,970,805 is EDA award ED25HDQ0G0009 to Huntsman, which has no USAspending record and whose execution the funding map says is not verified, so the page names its recipient and never calls it executed (corrected 2026-09-29 from "every dollar on an executed line"). The bar labels and the source line are written into the data file and read from there; only an award with no unverified line and nothing unassigned may say executed, and the source line names the exception to “verified against the signed federal Notices of Award” (corrected 2026-09-29). The award chart's subtitle says the solid bars are money named on a signed line and names Huntsman's $6.0M in the EDA bar as not verified as executed. The EDA bar's label is asserted whole, its $6.0M recomputed from the funding map's no-record line, so a label carrying any other amount fails (2026-09-30).
claims.source: funding-map/data/funding.json meta.outlays.no_record and meta.provenance[0], against scorecard.json delivery and group B rows
claims.assert: (lambda nr, dl, rows: nr['awardId'] == 'ED25HDQ0G0009' and nr['amount'] == 5970805 and 'not verified' in D['fm']['meta']['provenance'][0] and dl['unverified'] == {'awardId': nr['awardId'], 'name': nr['name'], 'amount': nr['amount'], 'source': 'eda'} and one(a for r in D['fm']['recipients'] for a in r['awards'] if a.get('awardId') == nr['awardId'])['programId'] == 'eda-direct' and dl['executed'] == dl['assigned'] - nr['amount'] == 73199371 and round(dl['executed'] / 1e6, 1) == 73.2 and all(n in rows['b-assigned']['definition'] for n in (nr['name'], 'no public record of its execution')) and 'not verified' in rows['b-eda']['sub'] and all('executed line' not in rows[k]['definition'] and 'executed' not in rows[k]['metric'] for k in ('b-assigned', 'b-recipients', 'b-ohio')) and all(('executed' in s['label']) == (s['unassigned'] == 0 and s['id'] != dl['unverified']['source']) for s in dl['sources']) and 'unverified' in one(s for s in dl['sources'] if s['id'] == dl['unverified']['source'])['label'] and one(s for s in dl['sources'] if s['id'] == 'eda')['label'] == '$%.1fM execution unverified' % (nr['amount'] / 1e6) and all(n in dl['source_note'] for n in ('Notices of Award', nr['awardId'], nr['name'], 'not verified')) and 'every line but one' in rows['b-disbursed']['definition'])(D['fm']['meta']['outlays']['no_record'], D['sc']['delivery'], {r['id']: r for r in D['sc']['rows']})
claims.actual: (D['sc']['delivery'].get('executed'), D['sc']['delivery'].get('unverified'), [(s['id'], s.get('label')) for s in D['sc']['delivery']['sources']], D['sc']['delivery'].get('source_note'))
claims.falsified_if: USAspending publishes ED25HDQ0G0009 (then the exception goes and every assigned dollar is executed, and this claim fails on purpose), another line loses its record, or a group B row goes back to calling the whole assigned total executed. The EDA bar read "every dollar on an executed line" in the round-2 draft of 2026-09-29 while the funding map said Huntsman's execution is not verified.

claims.text: Hero card 3, the band-2 headline and the chart title: $6.2 million has no named recipient yet, all of it Ohio money, held in two workstreams; the EDA and APEX awards are fully assigned and APEX is committed in a single line. The band-2 lede tells the two gaps apart: the PIC Translational R&D balance is not yet sub-granted, while the startup-support balance is delivered through Bounce Innovation Hub under a sub-grant agreement dated 15 May 2025, and the register names recipients there only for the nine $25,000 cohort awards (corrected 2026-09-29 from both workstreams' sub-grants "have not been signed yet").
claims.source: PIC award register, funding-map/data/funding.json, programme-to-source join recomputed from the sources and programs arrays
claims.assert: (lambda oh: sum(a['amount'] for r in D['fm']['recipients'] for a in r['awards'] if a['programId'] in oh) == 25084392)([p['id'] for p in D['fm']['programs'] if p['sourceId'] == 'ohio']) and one(s for s in D['fm']['sources'] if s['id'] == 'ohio')['award'] == 31250000 and D['sc']['delivery']['unassigned'] == 6165608 and sorted(g['id'] for g in D['sc']['delivery']['gaps']) == ['oh-rd', 'oh-startup'] and all(s['unassigned'] == 0 for s in D['sc']['delivery']['sources'] if s['id'] != 'ohio') and len([a for r in D['fm']['recipients'] for a in r['awards'] if a['programId'] == 'apex-workforce']) == 1 and 'not yet sub-granted' in one(p for p in D['fm']['programs'] if p['id'] == 'oh-rd')['note'] and 'Bounce sub-grant' in one(p for p in D['fm']['programs'] if p['id'] == 'oh-startup')['note'] and len([x for x in D['fm']['meta']['provenance'] if 'Bounce Innovation Hub under a subgrant agreement dated 15 May 2025' in x]) == 1 and [a['amount'] for r in D['fm']['recipients'] for a in r['awards'] if a['programId'] == 'oh-startup'] == [25000] * 9
claims.actual: [(g['id'], g['gap']) for g in D['sc']['delivery']['gaps']]
claims.falsified_if: A sub-grant executes under PIC Translational R&D or startup support, which is the expected way this number moves and should move it down; or an EDA or APEX line is de-obligated, which would put unassigned money outside Ohio and falsify the word 'all'. A third workstream developing a gap also breaks it: the sentence says two. Or the Bounce sub-grant is re-dated or stops covering the startup workstream, or the cohort count moves off nine awards of $25,000: the lede tells the startup balance apart from the R&D balance on exactly those facts.

claims.text: Row b-eda: EDA signed seven implementation awards, $51,001,413, and USAspending confirms the obligation to the project lead on six of them; the seventh, $5,970,805 to Huntsman, is not verified, so the row reads 6 of 7 against a target of all 7 awards confirmed and neither cell says all seven are obligated (corrected 2026-09-29 from “7 of 7”; the target corrected 2026-09-30 from “7 signed awards”, which counted signed awards against a current cell counting confirmed ones).
claims.source: Signed federal Notices of Award, via federal-money/data/techhub.json and cross-checked against the funding map's own eda-direct lines
claims.assert: (lambda r, nr: len(D['th']['leads']) == 7 and D['th']['award'] == 51001413 and sum(a['amount'] for r2 in D['fm']['recipients'] for a in r2['awards'] if a['programId'] == 'eda-direct') == 51001413 and one(s for s in D['sc']['delivery']['sources'] if s['id'] == 'eda')['pct'] == 100.0 and one(a for r2 in D['fm']['recipients'] for a in r2['awards'] if a.get('awardId') == nr['awardId'])['programId'] == 'eda-direct' and r['current'] == '%d of %d' % (len(D['th']['leads']) - 1, len(D['th']['leads'])) and r['target'] == 'all %d awards confirmed' % len(D['th']['leads']) and all('7 of 7' not in r[k] for k in ('current', 'target', 'sub')) and 'confirmed' in r['metric'] and all(n in r['sub'] for n in (nr['name'], 'not verified')))(one(x for x in D['sc']['rows'] if x['id'] == 'b-eda'), D['fm']['meta']['outlays']['no_record'])
claims.actual: (len(D['th']['leads']), D['th']['award'], [(x['current'], x['target'], x['sub']) for x in D['sc']['rows'] if x['id'] == 'b-eda'])
claims.falsified_if: An eighth implementation award appears, one of the seven is restated, the two files stop agreeing to the dollar, or USAspending publishes ED25HDQ0G0009 (then the row reads 7 of 7 and this claim fails on purpose). The row printed 7 of 7 in the round-2 draft of 2026-09-29 while its own sub said one line was not verified.

claims.text: Row b-ohio: 80.3 percent of the $31,250,000 Ohio Innovation Hub grant, $25,084,392, is on an executed line with a named recipient. Its definition names the programme aggregates on the state grant, the Polymer Pilot Facility and the state share of regional workforce programs, $20,009,985 of the numerator (corrected 2026-09-29 from "naming the organisation that holds them").
claims.source: Executed state grant agreement SBIG20251005 and its workstream budget, via funding-map/data/funding.json
claims.assert: (lambda o: tofixed(o['pct'], 1) == '80.3' and o['assigned'] == 25084392 and o['award'] == 31250000 and o['assigned'] + o['unassigned'] == o['award'])(one(s for s in D['sc']['delivery']['sources'] if s['id'] == 'ohio')) and (lambda oh: sum(a['amount'] for r in D['fm']['recipients'] if r['id'] in ('polymer-pilot-facility', 'regional-workforce') for a in r['awards'] if a['programId'] in oh) == 20009985)([p['id'] for p in D['fm']['programs'] if p['sourceId'] == 'ohio']) and (lambda df: 'naming the organisation' not in df and 'programme aggregate' in df and all(n in df for n in ('Polymer Pilot Facility', 'regional workforce programs'))) (one(r for r in D['sc']['rows'] if r['id'] == 'b-ohio')['definition'])
claims.actual: one(s for s in D['sc']['delivery']['sources'] if s['id'] == 'ohio')
claims.falsified_if: Any Ohio workstream sub-grant executes, which moves the share up, or the state restates a workstream budget. Printed to a tenth with toFixed, so 80.24 or 80.36 breaks it; 80.35 does not, because its binary value sits just below the half and still prints 80.3.

claims.text: Row b-secured: $106.3 million secured, being $85.3 million in awards plus $21.0 million in committed match and cost share.
claims.source: PIC award register, funding-map/data/funding.json meta totals
claims.assert: D['fm']['meta']['totals']['total'] == 106290451 and D['fm']['meta']['totals']['awards'] + D['fm']['meta']['totals']['match'] == D['fm']['meta']['totals']['total'] and D['sc']['delivery']['secured'] == 106290451 and D['sc']['delivery']['match'] == 20954667
claims.actual: D['fm']['meta']['totals']

claims.text: Row b-recipients: 21 named recipients hold award lines across seven programmes.
claims.source: PIC award register, funding-map/data/funding.json
claims.assert: len(D['fm']['recipients']) == 21 and len(D['fm']['programs']) == 7 and len([r for r in D['fm']['recipients'] if not r['awards']]) == 0 and all(n in one(r for r in D['sc']['rows'] if r['id'] == 'b-recipients')['definition'] for n in ('Two of them', one(r for r in D['fm']['recipients'] if r['id'] == 'polymer-pilot-facility')['name'], one(r for r in D['fm']['recipients'] if r['id'] == 'regional-workforce')['name'].lower())) and 'executed' not in one(r for r in D['sc']['rows'] if r['id'] == 'b-recipients')['metric'] + one(r for r in D['sc']['rows'] if r['id'] == 'b-recipients')['definition']
claims.actual: (len(D['fm']['recipients']), len(D['fm']['programs']))
claims.falsified_if: A recipient is added or removed. Two of the twenty-one, the Polymer Pilot Facility and regional workforce programs, are programme aggregates rather than single organisations, which the row's definition names; if the register ever splits one into named organisations the count rises and the definition needs rewriting, not just the number. The definition read 'One row of the register is a programme aggregate' until 2026-09-29. The metric read 'Named recipients under an executed agreement' until 2026-09-29; one of the 21, Huntsman, holds a line whose execution no public record confirms.

claims.text: Hero card 4, row c-polymer and the closer: 63 polymer credentials were awarded in the region in 2023, against a three-year average of 60, up in both years since 2021.
claims.source: IPEDS completions through 2023 at three regional institutions, via occupations/data/viz-data.json
claims.assert: sum(p['latest'] for p in D['occ']['programs'] if p['group'] == 'polymer') == 63 and D['occ']['program_totals']['polymer_awards_latest'] == 63 and D['occ']['program_totals']['latest_year'] == 2023 and D['sc']['talent']['polymer'][-1]['n'] == 63 and D['sc']['talent']['polymer_window'] == [54, 62, 63] and round(sum(D['sc']['talent']['polymer_window']) / 3) == 60 and len(D['occ']['program_totals']['institutions']) == 3 and D['sc']['talent']['polymer_trend'] == 'up in both years since 2021' and D['sc']['talent']['polymer_window'][0] < D['sc']['talent']['polymer_window'][1] < D['sc']['talent']['polymer_window'][2]
claims.actual: (sum(p['latest'] for p in D['occ']['programs'] if p['group'] == 'polymer'), D['sc']['talent']['polymer_window'])
claims.falsified_if: An IPEDS revision moves any of the three window years, a newer completions year is fetched, or the occupations page re-classifies a CIP code between its polymer and materials groups. This page inherits that classification rather than making its own, so a change there changes this number without any edit here. The window average read 80 until 2026-08-31: the window's first year turned out to be the wrong year and one year of the three was missing entirely. See _data/build/ipeds_mirror_fix.py.

claims.text: The talent chart annotation: credentials more than halved in 2021, from 124 to 54.
claims.source: IPEDS completions by year, occupations/data/viz-data.json programs.by_year
claims.assert: sum(p['by_year'].get('2020', 0) for p in D['occ']['programs'] if p['group'] == 'polymer') == 124 and sum(p['by_year'].get('2021', 0) for p in D['occ']['programs'] if p['group'] == 'polymer') == 54 and 54 * 2 < 124 and (lambda s: min(range(1, len(s)), key=lambda i: s[i]['n'] - s[i - 1]['n']) == [p['year'] for p in s].index(2021))(D['sc']['talent']['polymer'])
claims.actual: [(y, sum(p['by_year'].get(y, 0) for p in D['occ']['programs'] if p['group'] == 'polymer')) for y in ('2019', '2020', '2021', '2022', '2023')]
claims.falsified_if: A revision lifts the year after the peak-to-trough fall above half the year before it, at which point 'more than halved' is wrong even if the fall remains large, or the steepest one-year fall in the drawn series stops being the one the annotation names. The chart finds that year rather than being told it, because the year moved once already: this annotation read 2022 until 2026-08-31, when the mirror's mis-dated years were re-filed. The counts are administrative and in the low hundreds, so a single institution's late filing can move them.

claims.text: The talent figure title and the chart's own accessible description: polymer credentials ran between 118 and 179 a year through 2020, averaging 142, then dropped to 54 in 2021 and recovered only to 62 and then 63. Every pre-drop year sits above the 2021 count.
claims.source: scorecard/data/scorecard.json talent.polymer, the drawn series with 2020 quarantined
claims.assert: min([p['n'] for p in D['sc']['talent']['polymer'] if p['year'] <= 2020]) == 118 and max([p['n'] for p in D['sc']['talent']['polymer'] if p['year'] <= 2020]) == 179 and round(sum([p['n'] for p in D['sc']['talent']['polymer'] if p['year'] <= 2020]) / len([p['n'] for p in D['sc']['talent']['polymer'] if p['year'] <= 2020])) == 142 and one(p for p in D['sc']['talent']['polymer'] if p['year'] == 2021)['n'] == 54 and one(p for p in D['sc']['talent']['polymer'] if p['year'] == 2022)['n'] == 62 and one(p for p in D['sc']['talent']['polymer'] if p['year'] == 2023)['n'] == 63 and min([p['n'] for p in D['sc']['talent']['polymer'] if p['year'] <= 2020]) > 54 and min(p['year'] for p in D['sc']['talent']['polymer']) == 2014 and [p['year'] for p in D['sc']['talent']['polymer']] == list(range(2014, 2024))
claims.actual: [(p['year'], p['n']) for p in D['sc']['talent']['polymer']]
claims.falsified_if: A revision moves the pre-drop low off 118 or the high off 179, or lifts 2021 above the lowest pre-drop year, at which point 'ran between 118 and 179 ... then dropped to 54' stops describing the drawn series. The mean is pinned too, because the title may be worded either way and a scalar standing in for a range has to be the range's own. The last clause requires ten consecutive years with no hole: the series carried a gap at 2020 until 2026-08-31, and the gap was an artifact of the mirror's dating rather than a missing year.

claims.text: Row c-bachelor: 6 bachelor-level polymer credentials in 2023, a three-year average of 8.3, running 8, 11 and 6 across the window rather than in one direction.
claims.source: IPEDS completions, bachelor-level rows of the polymer CIP codes, via occupations/data/viz-data.json
claims.assert: D['sc']['talent']['bachelor_window'] == [8, 11, 6] and D['sc']['talent']['bachelor_trend'] == 'volatile' and sum(p['by_year'].get('2023', 0) for p in D['occ']['programs'] if p['group'] == 'polymer' and p['award'] == 'Bachelor') == 6 and round(sum(D['sc']['talent']['bachelor_window']) / 3, 1) == 8.3
claims.actual: D['sc']['talent']['bachelor_window']
claims.falsified_if: Any of the three window values moves. The row's direction word is computed from those three rather than typed, which is the fix for the sentence this claim used to guard: it read 'down in each of the three years' against a window that, once the mirror's mis-dated years were re-filed, runs 8, 11, 6. With counts this small a single programme's filing decides it: six is a number of people, not a rate.

claims.text: Row c-materials and the band-3 lede: materials credentials ran 29, 21 and 33 across the same three years, ending higher than they started while polymer credentials stayed near their low.
claims.source: IPEDS completions, materials CIP codes at the same institutions, via occupations/data/viz-data.json
claims.assert: D['sc']['talent']['materials_window'] == [29, 21, 33] and D['sc']['talent']['materials_window'][-1] > D['sc']['talent']['materials_window'][0] and D['sc']['talent']['materials_trend'] == 'volatile' and sum(p['latest'] for p in D['occ']['programs'] if p['group'] == 'materials') == 33 and D['sc']['talent']['materials_window'][-1] > D['sc']['talent']['polymer_window'][-1] / 2
claims.actual: (D['sc']['talent']['materials_window'], D['sc']['talent']['polymer_window'])
claims.falsified_if: The materials window stops ending above where it starts, or its direction word stops being computed from the three values. The sentence read 'rose from 20 to 33, moving opposite to polymer' until 2026-08-31; on the corrected years the window is 29, 21, 33 and polymer rises too, so neither the monotone rise nor the opposition survived and both went. One of the two materials programmes began reporting inside this window, so part of the movement is a programme appearing rather than growth.

claims.text: The chart's limitation note: the federal mirror behind this series filed 2020, 2021 and 2022 a year late and never served one collection year at all, so those three years are read from the NCES completions files instead. The window this page publishes is unchanged and is now three consecutive years rather than two years and a gap.
claims.source: occupations/data/viz-data.json programs.by_year, read as shipped
claims.assert: D['sc']['talent']['source_correction']['year_backfilled'] == 2022 and D['sc']['talent']['window'] == [2021, 2022, 2023] and [p['year'] for p in D['sc']['talent']['polymer']] == list(range(2014, 2024)) and sum(p['by_year'].get('2020', 0) for p in D['occ']['programs'] if p['group'] == 'polymer') == 124 and not [p for p in D['occ']['programs'] if p['by_year'].get('2019') is not None and p['by_year'].get('2019') == p['by_year'].get('2020')] and 'NCES completions files' in D['sc']['meta']['excludes']
claims.actual: (D['sc']['talent']['source_correction'], D['sc']['talent']['window'], [p['year'] for p in D['sc']['talent']['polymer']])
claims.falsified_if: The correction is reverted, the drawn series loses a year again, or the 2019 and 2020 counts return to being identical programme by programme. This page found the duplicated year before any gate did and compensated for it by reading a later window; what it could not see was that the duplicate was the first of three years filed late, and that the mirror's catch-up skipped a collection year outright. The window it published was right the whole time and one of the three years in it was the wrong year.

claims.text: Row d-emp: 18,594 plastics and rubber jobs across the twelve PIC counties in 2024.
claims.source: BLS QCEW 2024, NAICS 326, PIC-12, via occupations/data/viz-data.json
claims.assert: D['occ']['region']['emp'] == 18594 and D['occ']['region']['n_counties'] == 12 and D['occ']['region']['year'] == 2024 and D['occ']['region']['naics'] == '326' and D['occ']['region']['footprint'] == 'PIC-12'
claims.actual: D['occ']['region']
claims.falsified_if: A QCEW revision moves the count by one job, or the footprint changes. The row sits in group D because a plant opening or closing moves it and no PIC decision does; if this number ever became something PIC could be held to, it would have to leave group D, which is a definition change rather than a data change.

claims.text: Row d-federal: federal prime-contract obligations under chemical and plastics/rubber manufacturing codes averaged $41.4 million a year across the seven completed fiscal years FY2019-FY2025, in 2025 dollars. Unfinished FY2026 is excluded.
claims.source: USAspending prime-contract obligations at place of performance, FY2019-FY2025, via federal-money/data/federal.json
claims.assert: round(sum(r['real'] for r in D['fed']['naics'] if 2019 <= r['fy'] <= 2025) / 7 / 1e6, 1) == 41.4 and sorted(set(r['fy'] for r in D['fed']['naics'] if 2019 <= r['fy'] <= 2025)) == list(range(2019, 2026)) and one(r for r in D['sc']['rows'] if r['id'] == 'd-federal')['current'] == '$41.4M a year' and one(r for r in D['sc']['rows'] if r['id'] == 'd-federal')['sub'] == 'FY2019-FY2025 average, seven completed years' and one(r for r in D['sc']['rows'] if r['id'] == 'd-federal')['metric'] == 'Federal prime-contract obligations, chemical, plastics and rubber codes, PIC-12'
claims.actual: (sum(r['real'] for r in D['fed']['naics'] if 2019 <= r['fy'] <= 2025) / 7, one(r for r in D['sc']['rows'] if r['id'] == 'd-federal'))
claims.falsified_if: A revision changes the rounded $41.4M average, a completed year is missing, or the rendered row retains a stale value or period. FY2026 must stay outside this completed-year comparison; the historical average does not establish recurring demand. The row's label read 'Routine federal obligations to regional polymer firms' until 2026-09-29; the codes are chemical as well as plastics/rubber, the recipients are any contractor performing in the counties, and a historical average does not make the spending routine.

claims.text: Row d-rank: Ohio is first among the fifty-one disclosed states on plastics and rubber employment, with 54,846 jobs.
claims.source: BLS QCEW by-industry 2024, NAICS 326, private ownership, via peers/data/peers.json
claims.assert: D['peers']['states']['326']['rank_emp'] == 1 and round(D['peers']['states']['326']['subject_emp']) == 54846 and D['peers']['states']['326']['of_disclosed'] == 51
claims.actual: (D['peers']['states']['326']['rank_emp'], D['peers']['states']['326']['subject_emp'], D['peers']['states']['326']['of_disclosed'])
claims.falsified_if: A 2024 revision moves another state above Ohio, changes Ohio's employment by one job, or a state cell goes undisclosed. Ohio's rank is a state-level fact that PIC's twelve counties are one part of, which is why the row is context and why nothing on this page treats it as delivery.

claims.text: The note beside the table: no owner cell names a person, and three targets are set, every one of them a ceiling fixed by a signed award document rather than an ambition.
claims.source: scorecard/data/scorecard.json — the owner and target columns as the derive script writes them
claims.assert: D['sc']['counts']['owners_assigned'] == 0 and D['sc']['counts']['targets_set'] == 3 and all(r['owner'] in ('not assigned', 'outside PIC') for r in D['sc']['rows']) and all(r['target'] == 'not set' or 'award' in r['target'] for r in D['sc']['rows']) and sorted(r['id'] for r in D['sc']['rows'] if r['group'] != 'D' and r['target'] != 'not set') == ['b-assigned', 'b-eda', 'b-ohio']
claims.actual: [(r['id'], r['owner'], r['target']) for r in D['sc']['rows'] if r['target'] != 'not set']
claims.falsified_if: An owner is written into the data file, or a target appears that is not traceable to a signed document. Both would be real progress for PIC and both would make this sentence wrong, which is the point of guarding an absence: the claim is designed to fail the day the absence ends.

claims.text: The distinction the page states once: group D is cluster context PIC does not control, it is never counted into the accountable total, and no figure on the page averages the two.
claims.source: scorecard/data/scorecard.json — the group and status fields, and the counts derived from them
claims.assert: len([r for r in D['sc']['rows'] if r['group'] == 'D']) == 3 and all(r['status'] == 'context' and r['owner'] == 'outside PIC' for r in D['sc']['rows'] if r['group'] == 'D') and all(r['status'] != 'context' for r in D['sc']['rows'] if r['group'] != 'D') and D['sc']['counts']['accountable'] == len([r for r in D['sc']['rows'] if r['group'] != 'D']) and D['sc']['counts']['rows'] == D['sc']['counts']['accountable'] + D['sc']['counts']['context']
claims.actual: [(r['group'], r['status'], r['owner']) for r in D['sc']['rows']]
claims.falsified_if: A context row is moved into groups A, B or C, or an accountable row is marked context. Either would let a regional number be read as PIC delivery, which is the failure this page is organised to prevent. It also fails if the two totals stop reconciling, because a row counted in both would be exactly the averaging the page refuses.

claims.text: The note under the scorecard and the Limitations: an award register records commitment, not payment, so no figure taken from it measures money spent; the federal ledger publishes outlays on seven of the eight federal lines, and no public figure covers the state grant or the whole $85,335,784, so the disbursement row is empty and reads 'no figure spans the register'.
claims.source: funding-map/data/funding.json meta.outlays (USAspending Total Outlays, read 2026-09-01) and the award lines' awardId and outlay fields; scorecard/data/scorecard.json meta.caution and row b-disbursed
claims.assert: (lambda o, c, fl: o['lines'] == 7 and len(fl) == 8 and len([a for a in fl if 'outlay' in a]) == o['lines'] and [a['awardId'] for a in fl if 'outlay' not in a] == [o['no_record']['awardId']] and o['not_federal']['awardId'] == 'SBIG20251005' and one(s for s in D['fm']['sources'] if s['id'] == 'ohio')['award'] == o['not_federal']['amount'] and round(o['outlaid']) == 11642402 and o['obligated'] == 48114979 and D['fm']['meta']['totals']['awards'] == 85335784 and 'outlays on seven of the eight federal lines' in c and 'the state grant or the whole $85,335,784' in c and 'no figure taken from it measures money spent' in c and 'no figure on this page' not in c and one(r for r in D['sc']['rows'] if r['id'] == 'b-disbursed').get('empty') == 'no figure spans the register')(D['fm']['meta']['outlays'], D['sc']['meta']['caution'], [a for r in D['fm']['recipients'] for a in r['awards'] if a.get('awardId', '').startswith('ED')])
claims.actual: (D['fm']['meta']['outlays']['lines'], D['sc']['meta']['caution'], one(r for r in D['sc']['rows'] if r['id'] == 'b-disbursed').get('empty'))
claims.falsified_if: The note says again that no figure on the page measures money spent, while group B prints $11,642,402 of federal outlays; the number of federal lines with an outlay moves off seven of eight; the state grant acquires a public drawdown figure; or the empty disbursement row stops saying why it is empty. Until 2026-09-29 the note read 'It records no payment, so no figure on this page is a measure of money spent', and the accountability page quoted it beside the same outlays. The sentence is built from the funding map's outlay block by derive_scorecard.py, so a new outlay record changes it rather than leaving it stale.

claims.text: The note below the hero: the chain page's published-member flag marks 38 of the 710 companies listed there.
claims.source: chain/data/chain-data.json, meta.neo_total and the member field of each company; the 785-to-710 correction is CORRECTIONS.md 2026-09-11, 'Chain geography and the invalid coverage comparison'
claims.assert: D['chain']['meta']['neo_total'] == 710 and len(D['chain']['companies']) == D['chain']['meta']['neo_total'] and sum(1 for c in D['chain']['companies'] if c.get('member')) == 38
claims.actual: (D['chain']['meta']['neo_total'], len(D['chain']['companies']), sum(1 for c in D['chain']['companies'] if c.get('member')))
claims.falsified_if: The chain page's regional count or its member flags change. The sentence read '38 of the 785 companies' until 2026-09-29: it was written in the same change that corrected the chain page from 785 records to 710, and kept the old denominator. The typed sentence is bound to the page by the counts entry below, which fails in tools/all.mjs's noun gate if '38 of the 710' leaves the page; this assertion only reads the data.

claims.text: The provenance line, the closing note and the Limitations: every figure on the page but one is built from public federal and state records and PIC's published award register; the exception is the member count, from PIC's published membership and company register. The repository carries no membership register, and its one per-company membership fact is the chain page's published-member flag. Corrected 2026-09-29: the page said it was built only from public federal and state data and carried no member data. Corrected 2026-09-29: the closing note said the eight filled rows compute from federal and state records; three of them read PIC's award register, and the note now credits it.
claims.source: scorecard.json meta.publicOnly and meta.source; chain/data/chain-data.json member flags; scorecard.json rows[].source
claims.assert: sum(1 for c in D['chain']['companies'] if c.get('member')) > 0 and 'no membership register' in D['sc']['meta']['publicOnly'] and 'chain page’s flag' in D['sc']['meta']['publicOnly'] and 'no member,' not in D['sc']['meta']['publicOnly'] and 'published-member flag' in D['sc']['meta']['source'] and 'PIC award register' in set(r['source'] for r in D['sc']['rows'] if r['status'] == 'public') and len([r for r in D['sc']['rows'] if r['status'] == 'public' and r['source'] == 'PIC award register']) == 3
claims.actual: (sum(1 for c in D['chain']['companies'] if c.get('member')), D['sc']['meta']['publicOnly'][:120], sorted(set(r['source'] for r in D['sc']['rows'] if r['status'] == 'public')))
claims.falsified_if: The Limitations deny member data while the chain flag is set, or the page claims public federal and state data alone while a filled row reads PIC's award register. The provenance sentence is bound by the counts entry: 'but one' must stand beside 'figure', which fails if the line reverts to an unqualified 'every figure'. The closing note is bound the same way: 'accountable rows compute' must stand beside 'award register'.
